apostasy-punishable.rationale: Ch. XV "The United Order": to children who leave the Saints, "Go where you please", and to members who apostatize and withdraw, "Go, and welcome" (15:226); the appendix of s2 has "If you want to apostatize, apostatize, and behave yourselves" (1:84).

ban-interest.rationale: Ch. XXVII: "Every man who has got cattle, money, or wealth ... should put it out to usury" (1:252); the law is not addressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: In October 1865 Young urged the Saints to "buy of nobody else but their own faithful brethren", a boycott aimed at merchants hostile to the church that closed non-Mormon stores (s7).

civilians-legitimate-targets.rationale: Ch. XXXI "War": slaying "men, women, and children" through a great army is murder, "the guilty will be damned for it" (7:137).

class-collaboration.rationale: Ch. XXVII: "Let the poor be honest, let the rich be liberal, and lay their plans to assist the poor", enriching themselves as they build the Kingdom (3:6).

clerical-rule.rationale: Ch. XII "The Priesthood" says the High Priesthood "rules, directs, governs, and controls", and Ch. XXXIX describes the Kingdom as ruled spiritually and temporally (9:87; 10:328).

consent-of-governed.rationale: Ch. XXXI says a community should "govern themselves by a republican system", "selecting a man from their midst to preside over them" (7:11).

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ch. XV "The United Order" and Ch. XXV describe a people organised "as a family" with property held by trustees, the co-operative stores being "a stepping stone" to the Order of Enoch (16:8; 13:2).

death-penalty.rationale: The territorial law in force from 6 March 1852, while Young was governor, provided that a person convicted of a capital crime "shall suffer death by being shot, hung, or beheaded" (s9, s3).

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Ch. XXXI "Political Parties": "opposition ... has ruined our nation"; a republic means "letting the people rule by their united voice, without a dissension" (10:190; 5:228).

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Ch. XXXI "Political Government" defines government as theocratic, officers holding "that power which proceedeth from the Almighty", and says every government is "under the control of the Almighty" (6:346-7; 7:144).

elective-rulers.rationale: Ch. XXXI says the people should "concentrate their feelings ... to select the best man they can find to be their President" (7:12-13); Ch. XXXI also says a good man might serve for life (6:345).

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: On 15 September 1857 he proclaimed that "Martial law is hereby declared to exist in this Territory" and that no person could pass in or out of it "without a permit" (s6).

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Ch. XXXI calls the Constitution a "sacred charter of freemen's rights" needing only "a few alterations of a trifling nature", and says Government has no right to make any law on religion (10:41; 8:324; 2:177).

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Governor Young signed An Act in Relation to Service on 4 February 1852, which authorized indentured servitude for enslaved African Americans (s4); the same session limited the vote to white men (s5).

equal-outcomes.rationale: Ch. XXV says inequality "shall cease on the earth" before the Saints finish their mission, yet says a people never can be equal in possessions, and Ch. XXVII says the Lord does not require the rich to give all to the poor (19:46; 4:29; 13:302).

filial-duty.rationale: Ch. XXIV: "It is a disgrace to every man and woman ... not to take care of their own relatives, their own poor" (8:145); parents are not named.

freedom-is-self-government-of-desire.rationale: Ch. XIX "Obedience and Free Agency": strict obedience is "the only way ... to become free", otherwise "we shall become slaves of our own passions"; Ch. XXXI: "Individual self-government lies at the root" (18:246; 10:19).

gradual-change.rationale: Ch. XXXI says the Constitution's framers could not give a thing perfect at first: "It is a progressive--a gradual work" (7:14); Ch. XXXIX says the Kingdom develops gradually.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ch. X says the Lamanites "have just as good a right to call it theirs today as any people", and it is the Saints' duty to feed them as "we are living on their possessions" (11:264); authority is not spelled out.

initiating-nondefensive-force-unjustifie.rationale: Ch. XXXI "War" calls war for glory or territory murder, yet Ch. XXXI also pledges to "pour out our best blood for the defense of every good and righteous principle" (7:137; 10:41).

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Appendix of s2 (J. of D. 1:254): "True capital is labor"; "It is the bone, sinew, nerve and muscle of man that subdue the earth, make it yield its strength", producing the shelter and comfort of civilized man.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Ch. XXVII says a man "has no right with property, which ... legally belongs to him, if he does not want to use it" (1:252); it speaks of property in general, land among it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Ch. XI "The Scriptures" takes the Bible "for our guide, for our rule of action", and Ch. XXXI wants laws framed by divine law as in a theocracy (13:236; 6:346-7).

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "we do not care a farthing whether he is a whig, a democrat ... or anything else"; the Saints vote for the man who upholds civil and religious liberty (13:149).

limit-population.rationale: Ch. XVII "Birth Control": it is "the duty of every righteous man and woman to prepare tabernacles for all the spirits they can", and he condemns checks on increase (4:56; 12:120).

local-production.rationale: Ch. XXVI "Thrift and Industry" prays that "we may be compelled to depend upon our own" manufacturing, and urges raising flax and sugar at home rather than importing (7:67; 10:226).

member-state-blocks-federal-overreach.rationale: Ch. XXXI says no State should fail to be "amenable to the general Government" and Congress could veto any state act that transgresses the bounds of right (7:13).

morality-needs-religion.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "In the sincere observances of the principles of true religion and virtue, we recognize the base, the only sure foundation of enlightened society and well-established government" (2:178).

more-religion-public.rationale: Ch. XXXIX and Ch. XXXI describe a Kingdom of God to give laws to every nation, with all acts of life under its rule "spiritually and temporally" (11:275; 10:328).

national-church-status.rationale: Ch. XXXI says the President should treat the Saints' religion as he does Methodism, Quakerism and the other isms, and praises the Revolution that threw off "established religion" (2:186; 2:170).

night-watchman-state.rationale: Ch. XXXI: a true republican government has "for its object the perfection of mankind in righteousness" (7:10); the Kingdom governs "spiritually and temporally" (Ch. XXXIX, 10:328).

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Ch. XIX has the Saints obey "every good and wholesome law", and Ch. XXXI puts God's law first and says they are "aliens to all unrighteous" administration (11:134; 10:41; 2:176).

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Ch. XVII: no law frees a sealed wife from a husband "if he honors his Priesthood" (8:345), so release rests on his fault.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Ch. XXII "Religious Education": "The Christian world is actually coming to the point that they will dismiss the Bible from their schools", which he faults (13:213).

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Ch. XXVII: "let the rich be liberal, and lay their plans to assist the poor"; Ch. XXXI: a man of means should give the poor work and become "a benefactor to his race" (3:6; 10:193).

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Ch. XXXI: a President should deal "even-handed justice to all, utterly regardless of the clamor of party", labouring for the rights of all "irrespective of sect or party" (5:126; 7:63).

one-spouse-at-a-time.rationale: Britannica says that having accepted plural marriage, Young "took more than 20 wives and fathered 47 children" (s3).

physical-labour-duty.rationale: Ch. XXII "The Body and the Mind": philosophers "should apply their bodies to more manual labor", and Ch. XXVI "Labor Indispensable" says Zion is built by manual labor (3:248; 3:122).

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "A republican government consists in letting the people rule by their united voice, without a dissension"; Ch. XXXI also holds that all would counsel alike on the mind of Christ (5:228).

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Ch. XXXI: many administrators "do not care any more about the Constitution and the laws" and "trample the rights of the people"; he speaks of "many of them", not all (5:231).

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Ch. XXXI: the Saints' position toward the Government is "to put down iniquity, and exalt virtue" and serve God first, "if this is higher law, so be it" (2:176).

premarital-sex.rationale: Ch. XVII "The Family": "I would rather follow her to the grave, and send her home pure, than suffer my daughter to be prostituted", and the defiler "should be cast down ... among the worst of felons" (2:322; 11:267).

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "I stand for Constitutional law, and if any transgress, let them be tried by it"; the Saints will be controlled by officers who are controlled "by the Constitution and laws" (10:109; 5:231).

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Ch. XXVII "Wealth": a man "has no right with property ... if he does not want to use it", and should hold no more than he can use "to do good to himself and his fellowman" (1:252).

racial-franchise.rationale: In February 1852 the legislature "stipulated that white men over 21 years of age could vote", and in the debates Young rationalized disqualifying Black men from the vote (s5).

recall-officials.rationale: Ch. XXXI says that if a governor "officiate unjustly, hurl them from office" (6:345).

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Ch. XI: "I do not believe in putting any man's interpretation upon" the Bible; Ch. XIX: "we do not wish to change his ordinances, but to observe them" (1:237; 16:31).

religious-exemptions.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "no power or authority in the Government can lawfully or righteously molest us" in our religion, and it "has no right to make any law concerning it, or to prevent the free exercise thereof" (2:177).

religious-nation.rationale: Ch. XXXIX: when the Kingdom covers the earth "all the people" will not "become Latter-day Saints"; Ch. XXXI: every class of worshipper protected (11:275; 6:342-3). Appendix of s2 (5:329): the Kingdom will "govern and protect in their rights the various classes of men, irrespective of their different modes of worship".

religious-offensive-war.rationale: Ch. XXXI "War": "God never institutes war ... they are the results of the acts of the children of men"; "if I had my wish, I should entirely stop the shedding of human blood" (13:149; 10:108).

remove-indigenous-peoples.rationale: Ch. X "The Last Days" says "let the Lamanites come back to their homes", that killing an innocent Indian is murder, and that they have as good a right to the land as any people (11:263-4).

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Ch. XXXI wants a President "contented to live as they live, be clothed as they are clothed", even "if he has nothing more to eat than potatoes and salt" (7:12-13); pay is not mentioned.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Ch. XXXI "Opposed to Corrupt Administrators of Law": "It is a pretty bold stand ... to say that they will not be controlled by the corrupt administrators" who trample the Constitution (5:231-2).

restrict-conversion.rationale: Ch. XXXI: every class of worshipper protected "in the privileges of worshiping who, what, and when they pleased"; Ch. VII says "you have the privilege of making your own choice" (6:343; 7:165).

revolution-legitimate.rationale: Ch. XXXI says the men of the American Revolution "were inspired by the Almighty, to throw off the shackles of the mother government", and that "the spirit of revolution goes on" (2:170; 8:157).

right-to-secede.rationale: Ch. XXXI "States' Rights": if a State may secede, "so has a Territory ... a county ... a family", giving "perfect anarchy"; the general government should never let any part claim to be free and independent (8:322; 7:13).

rule-by-example.rationale: Ch. XXXI: the President and all officers "be patterns for the people to imitate", and "I do it by telling them the truth and letting them do just as they have a mind to" (2:183; 14:162).

separate-church-state.rationale: Britannica: he became governor of the provisional State of Deseret in 1849 while heading the church, and as church president "effectively ruled the people of Utah until his death" (s3).

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Ch. XVII "The Husband": "Let the father be the head of the family, the master of his own household"; wives and children "be subject to his dictates" (4:55).

simple-living.rationale: Ch. XV: "never want a thing you cannot get, live within your means"; Ch. XVIII condemns extravagance and waste in dress and housekeeping (16:11; 14:105).

single-common-good.rationale: Ch. XXXI says a republic is "learning what is for the best, and unitedly doing it", not standing on party opposition (5:228).

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Ch. XXXI: the Constitution "is a progressive--a gradual work", with later generations to build on its foundation (7:14), and the Saints will honour every wholesome government and law (10:41).

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Ch. XXXI "Fitness of Rulers": "No being is fit to rule ... until he has been controlled ... has yielded obedience to law" (8:324); he stands for Constitutional law with transgressors tried by it (10:109).

spiritual-nature.rationale: Ch. XXXI: a theocratic government is one whose officers "possess that power which proceedeth from the Almighty", with laws "enacted and executed in righteousness" (6:346-7).

state-harmful.rationale: Ch. XXXI backs "a true republican government" under a constitution, and says splitting from the Union would end in "perfect anarchy" (7:10; 8:322).

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Ch. XXII "Education" asks schools to employ teachers who are Saints "in principle", and regrets that the world will "dismiss the Bible from their schools" (10:225; 13:213).

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Ch. XXXI: a true republican government has "for its object the perfection of mankind in righteousness", and a civilization will lead people "to observe the laws Heaven has laid down" (7:10; 12:287).

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Britannica records the church president serving as governor of Deseret from 1849 and, even after being replaced, effectively ruling Utah's people as church president (s3).

term-limits.rationale: Ch. XXXI questions the eight-year limit on a President and would keep the best man in office as long as he serves (6:345).

territorial-expansion.rationale: Ch. XXXI: to make war on an innocent people "to possess myself of their territory" would make one guilty of murder (7:137); other kinds of expansion are not addressed.

traditional-family.rationale: Ch. XVII: "Let every man ... take a wife" and work to provide for her and the children, which "would produce results ... of incalculable good"; the father is head of the household (12:194-5; 4:55).

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Ch. XXXI: "The Gospel covenants are for those who believe and obey; municipal laws are for both Saint and sinner" (6:343).

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Ch. XXXI: the Saints "become aliens to all unrighteous, unjust and unlawful administrators", and God's law comes first: "If this is higher law, so be it" (10:41; 2:176).

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ch. XXXI asks whether it would not be better to extend the presidency "during life or good behavior" and continue the best man "as long as he will serve" (6:345).

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ch. XXVII: in a depraved society wealth opens "unrighteous monopolies, by which the poor are robbed and oppressed", dividing "society into castes" and subverting "every wholesome law" (10:3).

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Ch. XVII: "There is no ecclesiastical law ... to free a wife from a man to whom she has been sealed, if he honors his Priesthood" (8:345).

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Ch. XXXI "Saints and Politics": "Are we a political people? Yes, very political indeed" (13:149).

women-organise-apart-from-men.rationale: Ch. XVIII: he tells the sisters to "establish your Relief Societies" and "organize yourselves" for business and for relief of the poor, though "under the direction of the brethren" (12:201; 12:171).

women-suffrage.rationale: Young and others backed the territorial act that gave Utah women the vote, "but not the right to hold office", passed with no dissenting votes (s8).

work-for-welfare.rationale: Ch. XXIV: "To give to the idler is as wicked as anything else"; Ch. XVIII: "don't relieve the idle, for relieving those who are able but unwilling to work is ruinous" (16:19; 12:171).

role: President of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints (1847–1877) and first governor of Utah Territory (1851–1858)
summary: Founder-governor of Mormon Utah, Young taught a "republican theocracy" in which church and civil rule are one, property is a stewardship held for use, and the people govern by a united voice rather than by party. He opposed secession and wars of conquest, backed the Constitution, and urged industry, home production and cooperative economy.
notes: Only words are used here: Widtsoe's selection of Young's sermons (s1) and the appendix of sermon excerpts in Rich's book (s2), so an answer is set only where a sermon states the position. His acts (plural marriage in practice, the 1852 Utah servitude law, Indian policy, the Utah War, the "blood atonement" sermons, the Perpetual Emigrating Fund, Mountain Meadows) are in no local text (see notFound); a later pass with sources on that record should test the answers on church and state, slavery, apostasy, indigenous peoples and war against it, because record outweighs words.
